findings.summary: test_west_cea_material_interpolation hardcodes the source as 'imas:hdf5?path=/home/ITER/mcintos/Code/imas-efit/tests/data/imas/WEST/machine/dd4-1-0' and dd_version="4.1.0" (:296-301) instead of extending the mechanism that already owns this capability: tests/test_imas_iron_read.py:30-46 resolves the same source through NOVA_WEST_SOURCE_MANIFEST and the curation manifest's west-dd4-1-0 row, reads dd_version from that row, and pytest.skip()s when the manifest is not mounted. The new test duplicates that resolution (it does not wrap or extend it), drops the skip guard, and so turns an absent mount into an error rather than a skip, which makes tests/test_magnetisation.py unrunnable on any host without this workstation's imas-efit checkout and contradicts the repo rule that dd_version is taken per dataset from the manifest rather than guessed. It also re-asserts the six segments and first-material shape that tests/test_imas_iron_read.py:88-100 already owns. Remedy: move the manifest-resolving fixture to tests/conftest.py and read both the path and dd_version from it.

The assertion 'float(jax.grad(h)(0.0)) == pytest.approx(ends[0], rel=2e-14)' compares two outputs of the code under test: at magnitude 0, nova/biot/magnetisation.py:193 selects end_reluctivity[0], so h(B) = B * ends[0] and the gradient is ends[0] whatever the returned polynomial coefficients are. Both sides therefore move together and the assertion cannot redden on a defect in the polynomial origin slope; the real origin guard is the independent check at :256 against 1/(mu0*mu[0]). It does still catch a regression in _coefficient's zero-magnitude branch, so it is worth keeping, but it must not be counted as the origin-slope evidence it reads as.

The fragment states its central result only as a table of scalars (knot error, join mismatch, minimum sampled H') and carries no graphic, although the claim it exists to make - that dH/dB is strictly positive and continuous through two inserted breakpoints - is a plotted relationship, and docs/figures/iron-core-magnetisation/icm-law-fit was granted as a write path but left empty. A trace of dH/dB against B over 0-12 T with the inserted knots and the held tail marked would show the ramps and the positive plateau directly, which the number 56.166964456 A/(m T) does not. This is the figure mandate the project applies to evidence records, and the fragment's own construction paragraph describes exactly the curve that should be drawn.
